title: Unmasking Conversational Bias in AI Multiagent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2501.14844v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Detecting biases in the outputs produced by generative models is essential to reduce the potential risks associated with their application in critical settings. However, the majority of existing methodologies for identifying biases in generated text consider the models in isolation and neglect their contextual applications. Specifically, the biases that may arise in multi-agent systems involving generative models remain under-researched. To address this gap, we present a framework designed to quantify biases within multi-agent systems of conversational Large Language Models (LLMs). Our approach involves simulating small echo chambers, where pairs of LLMs, initialized with aligned perspectives on a polarizing topic, engage in discussions. Contrary to expectations, we observe significant shifts in the stance expressed in the generated messages, particularly within echo chambers where all agents initially express conservative view

translated_title: 揭示AI多智能体系统中的对话偏见
translated_abstract: 检测生成模型输出中的偏见对于降低其在关键场景中应用时的潜在风险至关重要。然而，现有的大多数识别生成文本偏见的方法都孤立地考虑模型，而忽视了其情境化应用。具体来说，涉及生成模型的多智能体系统中可能出现的偏见仍未得到充分研究。为填补这一空白，我们提出了一个框架，旨在量化对话式大型语言模型（LLMs）多智能体系统中的偏见。我们的方法涉及模拟小型回音室，其中成对的LLMs以对极化话题的一致视角初始化后进行讨论。与预期相反，我们观察到生成消息中表达立场的显著转变，尤其是在所有智能体最初都表达保守观点的回音室内。
tldr: 本文提出一个量化对话LLM多智能体系统偏见的框架，通过模拟回音室发现，即使初始立场一致，智能体讨论中立场也会发生显著转变，揭示了多智能体交互中的动态偏见现象。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a framework to quantify biases in multi-agent systems of conversational LLMs, revealing through echo-chamber simulations that stance shifts significantly during discussions even with aligned initial perspectives, uncovering dynamic biases in multi-agent interactions.
